method: Every contradiction and gap in E:/Droppy/port/porting/critiques/providers-and-protocols.md was adjudicated by reading full ranges of the pinned Swift source. First-pass reports were not used as evidence. All line numbers below were produced by `cat -n` / `grep -n` on the pinned checkout.

resolutions.finding: C1: sendsVersion: false omits the `jsonrpc` member (R042/R044 left it unresolved)
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. JSONRPC.swift:109, inside `private func write(_ message: [String: JSONValue])`: `if sendsVersion { message["jsonrpc"] = "2.0" }`. The flag controls exactly one thing: whether the literal string member `"jsonrpc": "2.0"` is added to every outbound frame (requests, notifications, responses and error responses alike, since all four go through `write`). It is NOT a client-version field. Declared JSONRPC.swift:48, set JSONRPC.swift:53-56. The file's own doc comment states it, JSONRPC.swift:39: `/// JSON-RPC 2.0 over a stdio process. Codex omits the `jsonrpc` member, ACP agents require it.` Call sites, counted by grep over the whole DroppyCode tree: exactly 3. (1) ACPSession.swift:117 `JSONRPCConnection(process: process, sendsVersion: true)`. (2) CodexSession.swift:508 `JSONRPCConnection(process: process, sendsVersion: false)`. (3) CopilotSession.swift:494 `JSONRPCConnection(process: process, sendsVersion: true)`. Codex is the only `false`. Two further details `write` applies to all three: `if message["params"] == .null { message.removeValue(forKey: "params") }` (JSONRPC.swift:107) drops the `params` key entirely rather than sending null, and `if isClosed { return }` (JSONRPC.swift:105) silently discards writes after close. Request ids are integers starting at 1 per connection (`nextID = 1`, JSONRPC.swift:49, incremented at :75).
resolutions.port_impact: The Windows port must build the envelope per connection, not globally. Codex `codex app-server` frames carry `{"id":N,"method":...,"params":...}` with NO `jsonrpc` member. ACP agents (cursor, opencode, grok, devin) and the Copilot SDK must receive `"jsonrpc":"2.0"` on every frame. The port must also reproduce the params-elision rule (omit `params` rather than send `null`) and the per-connection integer id counter starting at 1, because at least one agent keys on id type.

resolutions.finding: C2: PlanLimits.Window.detail looks unused; R041 asks who sets it, R040 answers for Z.ai; never reconciled
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. `var detail: String? = nil` is declared at PlanLimits.swift:10 with a default, and is never assigned anywhere inside PlanLimits.swift. Counting every `PlanLimits.Window(` construction in the tree there are 11 producing sites, and exactly 2 of them pass `detail:`, both in ZaiAPI.swift: line 133 `detail: "\(formatCount(current)) of \(formatCount(usage)) credits"` (for entry types "CREDIT_LIMIT" and "TOKENS_LIMIT", id `credit-<n>`) and line 142 `detail: "\(formatCount(current)) of \(formatCount(usage)) calls"` (for entry type "TIME_LIMIT", id `tools-<n>`, title literal "Monthly · MCP tools"). The other 9 sites leave it nil: AntigravitySession.swift:570, :592, :604, :616; CodexSession.swift:418; CommandCodeAPI.swift:91; CopilotSession.swift:457; PiPlanLimits.swift:94; PlanLimits.swift:307, :319, :325 (that is 11 total constructions, 2 with detail). The single consumer is UsageViews.swift:163 `if let detail = window.detail {`. So the field is live, not dead, but Z.ai is its only producer.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must keep `detail` on the window model and render it only when present. It must produce it for Z.ai alone, with those two exact formats including the word order and the plural nouns `credits` / `calls`, and must NOT invent detail strings for Codex, Claude, Copilot, Command Code, Antigravity or Pi windows.

resolutions.finding: C3: which readers call PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes:) (R041 asks; R040/R042/R045 each name one)
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Declared nonisolated at PlanLimits.swift:92. Call sites, counted by grep over the whole tree: exactly 3. (1) CodexSession.swift:416 `var title = PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes: window["windowDurationMins"]?.int)` then `if let name { title += " · \(name)" }` at :417 where `name` is `snapshot["limitName"]` and is non-nil only when `snapshots.count > 1` (:413). (2) PiPlanLimits.swift:96 `title: "Codex · " + PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes: windowSeconds / 60)` where windowSeconds is `raw["limit_window_seconds"]?.int` (:84). (3) ZaiAPI.swift:122 `title = PlanLimitsReader.windowTitle(minutes: minutes)`. The function body verbatim (PlanLimits.swift:92-102): nil -> "Usage limit"; 300 -> "5-hour limit"; 1_440 -> "Daily"; 10_080 -> "Weekly"; 40_320...44_640 -> "Monthly"; default -> `minutes % 1_440 == 0 ? "\(minutes / 1_440)-day limit" : "\(max(1, minutes / 60))-hour limit"`. Note the Monthly case is an inclusive ClosedRange of 28 to 31 days expressed in minutes, and the default branch's hour form clamps to a minimum of 1.
resolutions.port_impact: Port `windowTitle` once as a pure function with those exact five literals, the inclusive 40320...44640 range, the `% 1440 == 0` day form and the `max(1, minutes/60)` clamp, and call it from exactly those three readers. Z.ai additionally derives `minutes` from a unit code: ZaiAPI.swift:113-119 maps unit 3 -> number*60, 4 -> number*1440, 6 -> number*10080, 5 -> number*43200, anything else nil, each only when `number > 0`; with nil minutes it falls back to "5-hour limit" for creditIndex 0 and "Weekly" otherwise (ZaiAPI.swift:123-127).

resolutions.finding: C4: R044's header claims session delete was verified live, but no session.delete call exists
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. The claim is in a doc comment, not code: CopilotSession.swift:22-26 reads `/// Verified live against \`copilot 1.0.83\` (protocol version 3): framing, ping, account auth, session /// create, resume and delete, commands, agent and permission modes, model and /// effort switching, rewind points, compaction and the event envelope.` A case-insensitive grep for `delete` across CopilotSession.swift returns exactly 3 hits: line 24 (that comment) and lines 1037 and 1042, which are unrelated (`apply_patch` envelope header parsing, the literal `"*** Delete File: "`). A grep for `session.delete` / `session/delete` across the whole DroppyCode tree returns nothing. Counting every `connection.request("session.` call in the file there are 12 distinct methods and none is delete: session.create / session.resume (:108), session.send (:199), session.commands.invoke (:204), session.abort (:242), session.history.compact (:247), session.history.listRewindPoints (:254), session.history.rewind (:260), session.permissions.setMode (:335), session.mode.set (:343), session.model.switchTo (:356), session.model.setReasoningEffort (:362), session.commands.list (:385), session.permissions.handlePendingPermissionRequest (:910). The comment records what a human exercised by hand against the CLI during development; the app never deletes a Copilot session. The header is therefore stale relative to shipped behavior, and nothing outside Services/Providers deletes one either.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must NOT implement Copilot session deletion. Copilot session state accumulates under the CLI's own store (`~/.copilot/session-state` on macOS per CopilotSession.swift:8; the Windows equivalent is whatever `copilot` itself picks) and Droppy Code never prunes it. Reproduce that, including the unbounded growth.

resolutions.finding: G1: ClaudeSession handshake argv is not a delta of the session argv
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Two entirely separate argument vectors. HANDSHAKE, ClaudeSession.swift:186-191, is a fixed literal of exactly 9 elements in this order: ["-p", "--input-format", "stream-json", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--no-session-persistence", "--setting-sources", "user,project,local"]. It contains no --include-partial-messages, no --permission-prompt-tool, no --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, no --permission-mode, no --model, no --effort, no --settings, no --mcp-config, no --strict-mcp-config, no --system-prompt-snapshot, no --agents, no --forward-subagent-text, no --disallowedTools, no --append-system-prompt, no --resume, no --session-id. It does not call `knownOptions(of:environment:)` at all. SESSION, ClaudeSession.swift:85-134, starts from a 13-element base ["-p", "--input-format", "stream-json", "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--include-partial-messages", "--permission-prompt-tool", "stdio", "--setting-sources", "user,project,local", "--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions", "--permission-mode", <permissionMode>] (note: `--permission-mode` plus its value make the 13th and 14th; the literal array as written is 13 tokens with permissionMode as the last) and then conditionally appends --model, --effort, --settings {"fastMode":true}, --mcp-config <path> --strict-mcp-config, --system-prompt-snapshot off, the Hydra flags, an always-present --append-system-prompt pair (:123-128), and finally either --resume <id> [--resume-session-at <anchor>] or --session-id <id>. The session argv never contains --no-session-persistence; the handshake argv always does. Handshake supporting facts: 20-second watchdog Task that calls `process.terminate()` (:193-196), `defer { watchdog.cancel(); process.terminate() }` (:197), and the probe frame `process.send(["type": "control_request", "request_id": "handshake", "request": ["subtype": "initialize", "hooks": .null]])` (:198) - request_id is the literal "handshake", not the `droppy-code-<n>` form used by a live session (:305).
resolutions.port_impact: The Windows port must spawn the catalog/command probe with that exact 9-token vector and nothing else. Launching it with the session vector would pass --permission-prompt-tool stdio (the CLI would then wait for a permission transport that the probe never services), --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, and would omit --no-session-persistence, leaving a junk session file behind on every model-catalog refresh. Keep the 20s watchdog and the double terminate (watchdog + defer). Keep the probe's request_id as the literal string "handshake".

resolutions.finding: G2: handshake() requires a non-nil `commands` array or it throws, which also kills the model catalog
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. ClaudeSession.swift:199-211. The loop filters for `message["type"]?.string == "control_response"` AND `message["response"]?["request_id"]?.string == "handshake"` (:201-202), then: `guard let response = message["response"]?["response"], let commands = response["commands"]?.array else { throw ProviderError.failed("Claude could not load its commands.") }` (:203-205), and returns `(models(in: response), SlashCommand.claudeCommands(commands))` (:206). If the stream finishes without such a frame it throws `ProviderError.failed("Claude's command discovery did not finish. Try again.")` (:208). The single caller for the catalog is ProviderRegistry.loadClaudeCatalog at ProviderRegistry.swift:501-505, which wants only `.models`: `return try? await ClaudeSession.handshake(executable: executable, directory: directory, environment: environment).models` with `let directory = FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` (:503). Because that is `try?`, the throw becomes nil, and at ProviderRegistry.swift:484 `if let list, !list.isEmpty` means the catalog is simply not updated and `attemptedCatalogs` is NOT inserted (:491) - so it is retried on the next ask rather than failing loudly. The second caller is loadCommands at ProviderRegistry.swift:714, whose `catch` stores `error.localizedDescription` into `commandErrors[key]` (:717-718) after evicting the map if it has reached 32 entries. So a CLI that answers initialize with `models` but no `commands` key yields no Claude model catalog and a visible command error, silently.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must reproduce the coupling exactly: one probe, one guard, `commands` missing => both outputs lost. Do not 'fix' it by splitting models from commands. Reproduce both error strings verbatim, including the trailing period and the "Try again." sentence: "Claude could not load its commands." and "Claude's command discovery did not finish. Try again." Reproduce the `try?`-swallow at the catalog caller and the fact that a failed probe leaves `attemptedCatalogs` unset so it retries.

resolutions.finding: G3: Copilot listModels skips models whose policy.state is "disabled"
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, with a line correction: the filter is CopilotSession.swift:408, not :407. `guard let id = model["id"]?.string, model["policy"]?["state"]?.string != "disabled" else { continue }`. That single guard drops two classes of entry: any model with no `id` string, and any model whose `policy.state` equals exactly "disabled". Full function, CopilotSession.swift:402-425: connects on a throwaway connection in `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` (:403), `defer { connection.close() }` (:404), sends `models.list` with an empty object params (:405), seeds the list with `ProviderRegistry.copilotAuto` (:406) which is `ModelOption(id: "auto", name: "Auto", detail: "Copilot picks the model for each request", isDefault: true)` (ProviderRegistry.swift:146). Per surviving entry it builds a `details` array: if `billing.multiplier` is a double it appends `"\(Int(multiplier))× premium requests"` when the value is integral, else `"\(multiplier)× premium requests"` (:410-412, the multiplication sign is U+00D7, not the letter x); if `policy.state == "unconfigured"` it appends "Enable it in your GitHub Copilot settings first" (:413-415). detail is `details.isEmpty ? nil : details.joined(separator: " · ")` (:419, U+00B7 with surrounding spaces). name falls back to id (:418). efforts come from `supportedReasoningEfforts` (:420), defaultEffort from `defaultReasoningEffort` (:421).
resolutions.port_impact: The port must apply the `!= "disabled"` filter, otherwise the model picker offers models the CLI will refuse. It must keep "unconfigured" models in the list (they are only annotated, not filtered), reproduce the integral-vs-fractional multiplier formatting, and use U+00D7 for the multiplier and U+00B7 for the detail joiner. The Auto row is prepended unconditionally and is never subject to the filter.

resolutions.finding: G4: Copilot readPlanLimits has no feature note - skip rules, percent formula, date fallback, second request
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, CopilotSession.swift:444-468 plus :470-475. Method `account.getQuota`, empty-object params (:447). The title table at :448 has exactly 3 tuples in this order: ("premium_interactions", "Premium requests"), ("chat", "Chat messages"), ("completions", "Code completions"). Per key the snapshot is read at `quota["quotaSnapshots"][key]` and SKIPPED when any of four conditions hold (:451-453): the snapshot is absent, the snapshot is JSON null, `isUnlimitedEntitlement` is exactly true, or `entitlementRequests` is not a double or is <= 0. Percent (:454-456): `let remaining = snapshot["remainingPercentage"]?.double; let used = snapshot["usedRequests"]?.double ?? 0; let percent = remaining.map { max(0, min(100, 100 - $0)) } ?? min(100, used / entitlement * 100)`. Note the asymmetry: the remaining-branch clamps both ends, the used-branch clamps only the upper end (a negative usedRequests would yield a negative percent). Window id is the raw key string, title the table string, resetsAt `snapshot["resetDate"]?.string.flatMap(parseDate)` (:461). `parseDate` (:470-475) tries a default `ISO8601DateFormatter()` first, then retries the SAME formatter instance after `formatter.formatOptions = [.withFullDate]`, i.e. a bare `yyyy-MM-dd`. If no window survives the whole read returns nil (:464) - not an empty PlanLimits, so no bars and no plan name are shown. Only then does it issue a SECOND request, `account.getCurrentAuth` (:465), read `authInfo.copilotUser.copilot_plan` (:466), and wrap it: `PlanLimits(planName: PlanLimitsReader.planName(plan).map { "Copilot \($0)" }, windows: windows)` (:467). `PlanLimitsReader.planName` (PlanLimits.swift:104-107) returns nil for nil/empty and otherwise uppercases only the first character: `raw.prefix(1).uppercased() + raw.dropFirst()`. So copilot_plan "individual" becomes planName "Copilot Individual"; a missing copilot_plan leaves planName nil while the windows still show.
resolutions.port_impact: Port all four skip conditions, both percent branches with their exact clamping asymmetry (do not add max(0,...) to the used branch), the two-attempt date parse with the `.withFullDate` retry, the nil-on-no-windows return, and the second getCurrentAuth round trip on the same connection before close. The `min(100, used/entitlement*100)` branch divides by `entitlement` which is already guaranteed > 0 by the guard, so no divide-by-zero guard is needed or present.

resolutions.finding: G5: Copilot authStatus non-happy paths undocumented
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, CopilotSession.swift:428-441. The function is `static func authStatus(...) async -> ProviderStatus.Auth` and never throws. Four outcomes: (1) `guard let connection = try? await connect(...)` fails -> return .unknown (:429-431). (2) `guard let result = try? await connection.request("account.getCurrentAuth", [:])` fails -> return .unknown (:433). (3) `guard let auth = result["authInfo"], !auth.isNull` - absent OR JSON-null authInfo -> return .signedOut (:434). (4) otherwise `.signedIn(account)` where `var account = auth["login"]?.string` (:435) may itself be nil, giving `.signedIn(nil)`. The no-access decoration (:436-439): `if auth["copilotUser"]?["access_type_sku"]?.string == "no_access" { account = (account ?? "GitHub") + " · no Copilot access" }` - note the fallback base string is the literal "GitHub" and the separator is space-U+00B7-space. The connection is closed by `defer { connection.close() }` (:432) placed AFTER the first guard, so a failed connect leaks nothing. Underlying connect (:477-503) launches argv ["--headless", "--stdio", "--no-auto-update", "--log-level", "error"] (5 tokens, :483) plus `MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments()` (:486), framing `.contentLength` (:492), sendsVersion true (:494), then a `ping` with `["message": "droppy-code"]` (:497) and requires `pong["protocolVersion"]?.int != nil` or it closes and throws ProviderError.failed("This `copilot` does not speak the SDK protocol. Update it with `copilot update`.") (:498-501, backticks are part of the user-visible string).
resolutions.port_impact: The port must distinguish 'cannot reach the CLI' (.unknown) from 'reached it, not signed in' (.signedOut). A Windows spawn failure, a missing `copilot.cmd` on PATH or a framing mismatch must map to .unknown, never .signedOut, or Settings will tell the user to sign in when the real problem is the executable. Reproduce the "GitHub" fallback base and the exact suffix " · no Copilot access", and the protocol error string with its embedded backticks.

resolutions.finding: G6: the opencode auth fallback is `result.succeeded ? .signedOut : .unknown`, not unconditional .signedOut
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, with a line correction: the fallback is ProviderRegistry.swift:789; line 780 is the U+25CF strip. Full branch, ProviderRegistry.swift:773-789. Command: `Shell.run(executable, ["auth", "list"], environment: environment, timeout: 20)`; a thrown/failed spawn returns .unknown immediately (:774). Output is `TextCleanup.stripANSI(result.output + result.errorOutput)` (:775). The credential section is taken by cutting at the first line containing the literal "Environment": `text.components(separatedBy: "\n").prefix { !$0.contains("Environment") }.joined(separator: "\n")` (:776) - a case-sensitive `contains`, not a prefix match. Credential lines are those whose whitespace-trimmed form starts with "\u{25CF}" (BLACK CIRCLE, U+25CF); the marker is removed with `dropFirst()` and the remainder trimmed of whitespace (:777-781). If at least one credential was found (:782-788) it takes the FIRST, strips a trailing " api" or " oauth" (the suffix test is `credential.lowercased().hasSuffix(suffix)` but `dropLast(suffix.count)` is applied to the original-cased string, and the loop runs over both suffixes in order so a name ending " api oauth" would lose both), and returns `.signedIn(credential.isEmpty ? nil : credential)`. Only when no U+25CF line was found does line 789 run: `return result.succeeded ? .signedOut : .unknown`.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must carry the exit status through to this decision. A non-zero `opencode auth list` (old CLI without the subcommand, broken install, wrong PATH entry) must surface as .unknown, not 'Not signed in'. Match on the literal U+25CF code point rather than on any bullet-looking glyph, and strip ANSI first - on Windows the CLI may emit VT sequences into a pipe. Keep the case-sensitive "Environment" section cut.

resolutions.finding: G7: the nine Command Code seed ids and names were never recorded, though they are a persisted identity and an equality key
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. `CommandCodeAPI.seed` is declared at CommandCodeAPI.swift:349-359 and aliased as `ProviderRegistry.commandcodeSeed` at ProviderRegistry.swift:150. Counting the literals: exactly 9 entries, in this order, with `efforts:` supplied by `CommandCodeAPI.efforts(for:)` (CommandCodeAPI.swift:283-310) and every detail separator being space-U+00B7-space. (1) id "claude-sonnet-5", name "Claude Sonnet 5", detail "Anthropic · best combo of speed & intelligence", efforts ["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"], isDefault: true. (2) id "claude-fable-5-1", name "Claude Fable 5.1", detail "Anthropic · most capable for demanding reasoning & long-horizon agents", efforts ["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]. (3) id "claude-opus-5", name "Claude Opus 5", detail "Anthropic · most intelligent Opus for agents and coding", efforts ["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]. (4) id "gpt-6-astra", name "GPT-6 Astra", detail "OpenAI · most capable OpenAI model for demanding reasoning & agents", efforts ["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]. (5) id "gpt-5.6-sol", name "GPT-5.6 Sol", detail "OpenAI · latest frontier model for general complex work", efforts ["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]. (6) id "google/gemini-3.8-flash", name "Gemini 3.8 Flash", detail "Google · newest Gemini Flash, improved core reasoning", efforts ["low","medium","high"]. (7) id "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", name "DeepSeek V4 Flash", detail "Open Source · fast hybrid-attention reasoning", efforts ["high","max"]. (8) id "moonshotai/kimi-k3", name "Kimi K3", detail "Open Source · long-horizon coding & knowledge work with 1M context", efforts ["low","high","max"]. (9) id "zai-org/glm-5.3", name "GLM 5.3", detail "Open Source · frontier coding with emergent cyber capabilities", efforts ["low","high","max"]. Only entry 1 sets isDefault. The critic's ids and names are correct in all 18 values. These matter twice: (a) the list is JSON-encoded whole into UserDefaults key "providerModelCatalogs" (ProviderRegistry.swift:670-672); (b) ProviderRegistry.swift:464 `|| (provider == .commandcode && models(for: provider) == Self.commandcodeSeed)` is a full structural `==` on `[ModelOption]`, so a re-probe is triggered only when every field of every one of the nine rows still matches - one wrong effort array or one changed detail string and the app stops recognizing the catalog as 'still the seed' and stops re-probing on launch.
resolutions.port_impact: Transcribe all nine rows byte-for-byte, including the ampersands, the U+00B7 separators, the '1M' capitalization and the effort arrays. The seed doubles as an equality sentinel, so any drift silently changes when the live catalog is fetched. The same pattern applies to the three sibling sentinels at ProviderRegistry.swift:463 (`== [Self.copilotAuto]`) and :465 (`== Self.piSeed`, where piSeed is the single row ModelOption(id: "default", name: "Default", detail: "The model pi itself is set to", efforts: ["off","minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"], defaultEffort: "medium", isDefault: true), ProviderRegistry.swift:153).

resolutions.finding: G8: Antigravity's runtimeMode/interactionMode are written every send and never read; the report called them 'refreshed on each send'
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, proven by exhaustive grep. Every occurrence of `runtimeMode` or `interactionMode` in AntigravitySession.swift: declarations :23 and :24; init writes :57 and :58; :88; the `modeArguments` signature :123 and its body :128, :135; send writes :150 and :151. There is no other occurrence. Line 88 reads the CONFIGURATION, not the properties: `arguments += modeArguments(runtimeMode: configuration.runtimeMode, interaction: configuration.interactionMode)`. Lines 128 and 135 are inside `modeArguments` and refer to its parameter, which shadows the property. Therefore the two stored properties are write-only after init: nothing in the class ever reads `self.runtimeMode` or `self.interactionMode`. `modeArguments` itself (:123-139) produces: ["--mode", "plan"] when interaction == .plan; otherwise [] for .supervised and ["--mode", "accept-edits"] for .autoAcceptEdits, .auto and .fullAccess; then appends ["--dangerously-skip-permissions"] when runtimeMode == .fullAccess. It is called exactly once, at :88, inside start(). There is a second, asymmetric fact the critic did not state: the sibling properties `model` and `effort` ARE written in send (:152-153) and ARE read in start (:85-87 via `Self.normalize(model: model, effort: effort)`). So the class stores four per-turn values, reads two of them at launch and never reads the other two. That asymmetry is in the source, not in the report.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must reproduce the behavior, not the intent: a mid-thread Supervised/Auto/Full-access change, or a Plan/Build toggle, cannot reach a running `agy` process. Only a session restart re-reads `configuration.runtimeMode`/`configuration.interactionMode`, and a restart picks up the UPDATED model/effort but the ORIGINAL modes. Contrast PiSession.swift:279-288 `writeGate(finalReport:)`, which serializes `runtimeMode.rawValue` and `interactionMode.rawValue` into the per-session gate JSON and is re-run every turn, so the same switch does take effect there. Carry the two dead properties across if you want a literal port, but do not wire them up - wiring them would change behavior.

resolutions.finding: G9: ACP applyConfigOptions nils effortConfigID and fastConfigID at the top of every call
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, ACPSession.swift:327-398. Lines 328-331 open the function: `var efforts: [String] = []`, `var hasFast = false`, then `effortConfigID = nil` and `fastConfigID = nil`. Crucially `modeConfigID` (:364) and `modelConfigID` (:338) are NOT reset - they are only ever assigned inside their branches, so they survive a partial update while the other two do not. Repopulation requires specific branches: `effortConfigID = id` only under `case "thought_level", "effort"` AND only after `guard Self.isEffortScale(scale) else { break }` (:367-374), where isEffortScale (:408-411) requires at least one value whose lowercase is in the 7-element set {"none","low","medium","high","xhigh","max","extra-high"}; `fastConfigID = id` only under `case "model_config"` AND only when `id == "fast"` (:375-380). The switch selector is `option["category"]?.string ?? id` (:336), so an agent that reports no category is matched on its option id. There are exactly 3 call sites: ACPSession.swift:278 (initial session state, `state["configOptions"]`), :484 (the reply to the app's own `session/set_config_option` request, :479), and :538 (the `config_option_update` session/update notification). Consequence at the consumer: :456 `if let effort, !effort.isEmpty, let effortConfigID, effort != currentEffort` and :460 `if let fastConfigID` - once nil, the app stops sending effort and Fast changes entirely.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce the reset and its asymmetry exactly, including the fact that mode and model ids survive a partial update while effort and fast do not. Do not 'repair' it by resetting all four or by resetting none - either change alters which sliders disappear.

resolutions.finding: G10: the ACP session/update kinds config_option_update, agent_thought_chunk, plan and available_commands_update are handled but never named
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, ACPSession.swift notification switch. `case "agent_thought_chunk"` :498-502 emits `.reasoningDelta(id:text:)` under a `thoughtID ?? nextID("thought")`. `case "plan"` :525-527 parses `update["entries"]` via `Self.parseTodoItems` and emits `.todos(steps)` unconditionally (unlike the tool_call todo path at :507-512 which only emits when non-empty). `case "available_commands_update"` :528-533 maps `availableCommands` entries requiring a `name`, with `detail: command["description"]?.string ?? ""`, and emits `.commands(commands)` - including an empty list, which clears the slash-command menu. `case "config_option_update"` :537-538 re-runs applyConfigOptions on `update["configOptions"]`, which per G9 re-emits `.models(models, current: currentModel)` (:397) with a possibly new current model, a new effort scale and a new fast tier. Neighbours in the same switch that are equally live: `current_mode_update` :534-536 (sets currentMode and emits `.modeChanged(currentMode == planMode ? .plan : .build)` only `if let planMode`), `session_info_update` :539-540 (emits `.title` only for a non-empty title), `usage_update` :541-549 (emits `.usage(ContextUsage(usedTokens:windowTokens:))` and deliberately does NOT charge the token ledger - see the comment at :543-547 explaining that `used` is context occupancy, not spend).
resolutions.port_impact: The port must treat the ACP agent as able to push a live model, effort or Fast-tier change mid-session, and must wire config_option_update through the same code path as the set_config_option reply (sharing the G9 reset). It must let available_commands_update clear the menu with an empty array, must emit todos from `plan` even when the parse yields nothing, and must NOT feed ACP usage_update into the spend ledger.

resolutions.finding: G11: OpenAICompatibleSession cancellation is uncovered - interrupt/stop/finishInterrupted and approveAllRemaining
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, with line corrections. `interrupt()` is OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:437-446 (critic said 437-446, correct): sets `interrupted = true`; `sendTask?.cancel()`; `roundTask?.cancel(); roundTask = nil`; `sseDrain?.cancel(); sseDrain = nil`; then `for (_, continuation) in pendingApprovals { continuation.resume(returning: false) }` and `pendingApprovals.removeAll()`. It does NOT nil sendTask (that happens in the task's own `defer` at :270). `stop()` is :471-482 (critic said 471-482 via a different anchor, correct in substance): everything interrupt does, plus `isStopping = true` first and `sessionID = nil` last, which is what flips `isRunning` false given `var isRunning: Bool { sessionID != nil && !isStopping }` at :240. `finishInterrupted()` is :808-812: resumes every pending approval with `false`, clears the map, and emits `.turnCompleted(status: .interrupted, error: nil)`. It is reached from five places: :283 (cancelled before the turn starts), :407, :414, :422 - plus :428 emits `.turnCompleted(status: .interrupted, error: nil)` directly. `approveAllRemaining` is set true at :450 inside `resolveApproval` when `optionID == "always"`, and reset to false at :292 at the top of every `performTurn`, alongside `interrupted = false` at :291. Therefore the 'always' option really is per-turn. Additional related fact: the in-flight tool bodies guard on `!Task.isCancelled, !interrupted` at roughly a dozen sites (:882, :895, :905, :913, :928, :932, :946, :950, :963, :984, :1007, :1020, :1078) and return the literal string "Stopped." to the model as the tool result.
resolutions.port_impact: This session type has no child process at all, so a Windows port cannot reuse the process-termination path. It must cancel the equivalent async work (the turn task, the round task, the SSE drain) and, critically, must resolve every outstanding approval promise as a DECLINE - an in-flight permission dialog is silently answered 'no' when the user hits stop. Reproduce the per-turn reset of approveAllRemaining so the 'Approve for turn' label stays honest, the `isRunning` composition from sessionID and isStopping, and the literal tool result "Stopped.".

resolutions.finding: G12: refreshCredits lacks refreshPlanLimits's watchdog and defer, and leaves creditsFetchedAt on an empty key
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, with a line correction: refreshCredits is ProviderRegistry.swift:621-640 (critic said 626-641). Body in order: guard `CreditsReader.exposesCredits(provider), !loadingCredits.contains(provider)` (:622); key selection where Command Code uses `CommandCodeAPI.apiKey(environment:) ?? ""` and everyone else `settings.apiKey(for:)` (:624-626); `guard !apiKey.isEmpty else { credits[provider] = nil; return }` (:627-630) - `creditsFetchedAt[provider]` is deliberately untouched here; the 60-second freshness check (:631); `loadingCredits.insert(provider)` (:632); then a bare `Task { let balance = await CreditsReader.read(...); loadingCredits.remove(provider); guard let balance else { return }; credits[provider] = balance; creditsFetchedAt[provider] = .now }` (:633-639). Compare refreshPlanLimits (:546-581), which for BOTH the API-key branch and the CLI branch creates `let watchdog = Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(25)); loadingLimits.remove(provider); drainedForcedRead(provider) }` (:557, :569) and wraps the work in `defer { watchdog.cancel(); loadingLimits.remove(provider); drainedForcedRead(provider) }` (:559, :571), and which queues a forced read that arrives during an in-flight one via `forcedLimitReads.insert(provider)` (:548) drained by `drainedForcedRead` (:584-587). refreshCredits has no watchdog, no defer, and no forced-read queue: a `force: true` call arriving while `loadingCredits` holds the provider is dropped outright at :622, and a `CreditsReader.read` that never returns leaves `loadingCredits` populated for the rest of the run.
resolutions.port_impact: Reproduce both asymmetries rather than unifying them: the credits spinner can hang where the plan-limits spinner cannot, a forced credits refresh during an in-flight one is a no-op, and clearing an empty key leaves the stale fetch timestamp so the very next non-empty call is still subject to the 60-second gate. On Windows a `CommandCodeAPI.apiKey` read that blocks on a slow network share would expose exactly this hang.

resolutions.finding: T1 (thin): R044's static half - listModels, authStatus, readPlanLimits at CopilotSession.swift:400-475
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. The range was re-read in full. Its three algorithms are now recorded above under G3 (listModels, :402-425), G5 (authStatus, :428-441) and G4 (readPlanLimits, :444-468 plus parseDate :470-475), together with the shared `connect` helper at :477-503 that all three use: argv ["--headless", "--stdio", "--no-auto-update", "--log-level", "error"] plus MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments(), framing .contentLength, sendsVersion true, a `ping` handshake carrying ["message": "droppy-code"], and a hard requirement that the pong carry an integer `protocolVersion`. All three static entry points run against `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` as the working directory and close the connection via `defer`.
resolutions.port_impact: Implement the three static reads against one shared connect helper exactly as the source does, including the temporary-directory working dir. Each read opens and closes its own process, so on Windows the port pays a `copilot` process spawn per Settings refresh, per catalog load and per usage-panel open - that cost is upstream behavior and must not be optimized away with a cached connection, because a cached connection would change when `models.list` reflects a plan change.

resolutions.finding: X1 (cross-cutting): three JSON-RPC dialects on one connection class, with different envelopes and framings
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Envelope: see C1 - exactly 3 JSONRPCConnection constructions, Codex alone with sendsVersion false. Framing, counted over the whole tree by grep for `framing:` outside StdioFramer.swift: the default is `.lines` (StdioProcess.swift:27 `framing: Framing = .lines`); exactly 1 site passes `.contentLength` (CopilotSession.swift:492); exactly 2 sites pass `.lines` explicitly (PiCLI.swift:56, PiSession.swift:117). Every other StdioProcess - ACP, Codex app-server, Claude, Antigravity, Command Code, the Claude get_usage probe in PlanLimits.swift:254 - takes the `.lines` default. So the critic's 'Pi and Command Code and Antigravity use line/JSONL framing instead' is right in effect though only Pi states it explicitly. The `.contentLength` framer (StdioFramer.swift:35-54, :71-80) splits on a literal "\r\n\r\n" separator and parses a case-insensitive `content-length` header, rejecting negative lengths; the `.lines` framer splits on a single 0x0A and, uniquely, returns any trailing unterminated buffer from `finish()` (:63-69) whereas .contentLength discards it.
resolutions.port_impact: The port needs one framer with two modes and one envelope switch, wired per connection: Copilot => contentLength + jsonrpc; ACP => lines + jsonrpc; Codex app-server => lines + NO jsonrpc; Pi, Command Code, Antigravity, Claude => lines (not JSON-RPC at all, their own message shapes). On Windows, the .lines framer must split on 0x0A only and must tolerate a preceding 0x0D being part of the payload, because the source splits on the byte and does not strip CR - a CLI that emits CRLF would hand a trailing 0x0D to the JSON parser. That is upstream behavior; JSONValue.parse tolerating trailing whitespace is what makes it work.

resolutions.finding: X2 (cross-cutting): -32601 messages differ by provider and must not be unified
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, with a line correction and one site the critic missed. Counting every -32601 in the tree: exactly 4 sites. (1) JSONRPC.swift:121 - the fallback inside `handle` when a request arrives and `onRequest` is nil: `respond(to: id, errorCode: -32601, message: "Method not found")`. (2) ACPSession.swift:557 (the critic said 559) - `guard method == "session/request_permission" else { connection?.respond(to: id, errorCode: -32601, message: "Method not found"); return }`. (3) CodexSession.swift:969 - `connection?.respond(to: id, errorCode: -32601, message: "Droppy Code does not support \(method).")`. (4) CopilotSession.swift:775 - the same interpolated string. So ACP answers the bare "Method not found" and the two others answer "Droppy Code does not support <method>." with a trailing period, and the connection-level default (site 1) also uses "Method not found" - it fires only for a connection whose `onRequest` was never set, which in this checkout is every catalog/auth/quota probe connection, since those pass `configure: { _ in }` (CopilotSession.swift:403, :429, :445; CodexSession.swift:501-509 callers).
resolutions.port_impact: Keep four distinct emission points, not one helper with one string. The app name appears inside two of the wire messages, so the Windows port's own product name must NOT be substituted there if exact parity is wanted - the string is literally 'Droppy Code does not support ' in the source.

resolutions.finding: X3 (cross-cutting): the droppy-code client identity rides four handshakes on different key paths
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. The critic named four carriers; counting the tree there are five distinct ones. (1) ACPSession.swift:127, inside the `initialize` request alongside `"protocolVersion": 1` and `clientCapabilities`: `"clientInfo": ["name": "droppy-code", "title": "Droppy Code", "version": .string(AppInfo.version)]`. (2) CodexSession.swift:518, inside `initialize` alongside `"capabilities": ["experimentalApi": true]`: the identical clientInfo object. (3) CopilotSession.swift:123, `"clientName": "droppy-code"` as a flat member of the session.create/session.resume params - no title, no version. (4) CopilotSession.swift:497, the ping payload `["message": "droppy-code"]`. (5) MISSED BY THE CRITIC: Claude carries it in two different places - live control request ids `"droppy-code-\(controlCounter)"` (ClaudeSession.swift:305, counter starts at 0 and pre-increments so the first id is "droppy-code-1"), and the standalone get_usage probe in PlanLimits.swift:274-281, which uses the fixed request ids "droppy-code-init" and "droppy-code-usage". Note the Claude catalog handshake does NOT use the prefix - it uses the bare literal "handshake" (ClaudeSession.swift:198). `AppInfo.version` resolves through Text.swift; the sibling `AppInfo.name` is `Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleDisplayName") as? String ?? "Droppy Code"` (Text.swift:4).
resolutions.port_impact: Five carriers to port, each with its own shape. Two are ids rather than fields and are parsed back by the app itself (ClaudeSession.swift:337-338 matches `pendingControl` by the id string; PlanLimits.swift:278-284 switches on the two literal ids), so they are a protocol contract with the app's own reader, not just a label - changing them breaks response routing. The Copilot `ping` message value is opaque to the CLI but the app requires `protocolVersion` back.

resolutions.finding: X4 (cross-cutting): RuntimeMode/InteractionMode rawValues are an on-disk contract with the shipped TypeScript
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Enums are declared outside this bundle, at Provider.swift:145-179 and :181-184. RuntimeMode is `String`-backed with exactly 4 cases and implicit raw values: supervised, autoAcceptEdits, auto, fullAccess. InteractionMode is `String`-backed with exactly 2: build, plan. PiSession.swift:279-288 `writeGate(finalReport:)` serializes a 4-key JSON object to the per-session gate file: "runtimeMode" (`runtimeMode.rawValue`), "interactionMode" (`interactionMode.rawValue`), "finalReport" (bool), "systemPrompt" (written as the empty string literal ""), written with `options: .atomic`. The shipped TypeScript in `PiCLI.extensionSource` compares against exactly 4 string literals: "plan" at PiCLI.swift:191 and :201, "fullAccess" at :202, "autoAcceptEdits" and "auto" at :204, "auto" again at :205. "supervised" and "build" are never compared - they are the fall-through that reaches the approval prompt. The comparison is `===` in TypeScript, so exact case matters.
resolutions.port_impact: The Windows port must keep the camelCase raw values byte-identical on both sides of the file. The gate file is the only channel, so a serializer that lowercases or snake_cases enum names (a common default in TS/JSON layers) would silently turn Full access into Supervised. Port the gate as a hand-written object literal, not through a generic enum serializer, and keep `.atomic` semantics (write-temp-then-rename) because the extension polls the file while the app rewrites it every turn.

resolutions.finding: X5 (cross-cutting): four 'install a helper file only when the bytes differ' patterns
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. There are exactly 3 install-if-differs writers, plus 2 per-session scratch directories (the critic bundled them as 'four patterns'). The 3 writers share one idiom verbatim - `let data = Data(<source>.utf8); if (try? Data(contentsOf: file)) != data { try data.write(to: file, options: .atomic) }` - and differ only in path and filename: (a) CommandCodeAPI.installMod(), CommandCodeAPI.swift:448-457, file `<AppSupport>/\(AppInfo.name)/CommandCode/droppy-code-approvals.ts`, base dir from CommandCodeAPI.swift:440-444. (b) PiCLI.installExtension(), PiCLI.swift:117-126, file `<AppSupport>/Droppy Code/pi/droppy-gate.ts`, base dir from PiCLI.swift:14-18 - note this one HARD-CODES the literal "Droppy Code" where the other two interpolate `AppInfo.name`. (c) MCPBridgeSource.installBridge(), MCPBridgeSource.swift:240-251, file `<AppSupport>/\(AppInfo.name)/MCP/droppy-mcp-bridge.mjs`. All three fall back to `<home>/Library/Application Support` when `FileManager.urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first` is nil. The 2 scratch directories: Pi gates at `PiCLI.supportDirectory/gates/<UUID().uuidString>.json` (PiSession.swift:86-89, cleared by setting `self.gateURL = nil` at :220), and Command Code approvals at `<...>/approvals` (CommandCodeSession.swift:105-108), removed wholesale in `stop()` via `try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: approvalDirectory)` (CommandCodeSession.swift:260-262).
resolutions.port_impact: Three writers and two scratch trees to relocate to `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (or wherever the port's data dir lives). The PiCLI hard-coded "Droppy Code" vs AppInfo.name split must be decided deliberately: a renamed Windows build that interpolates its own name everywhere will put the Pi extension in a different folder than the source would, and since the path is handed to `pi -e <path>` at launch that is behavior-visible only in where the file lands. The byte-compare-before-write is what keeps a new build's helper from being rewritten on every launch; keep it, and keep the atomic write, because the CLI may be reading the file concurrently.

resolutions.finding: X6 (cross-cutting): runtime-mode changes reach providers three ways and only some survive without a restart
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Live protocol call: Claude sends `["subtype": "set_permission_mode", "mode": .string(mode)]` in send() when the computed mode differs (ClaudeSession.swift:217-221) and again after an ExitPlanMode approval (:264-266); Copilot sends `session.permissions.setMode` (:335) and `session.mode.set` (:343) from applyModes; ACP sends `session/set_config_option` for the mode option when `modeConfigID` is known (ACPSession.swift:468-469); Codex carries approval/sandbox policy per turn in its thread params. Rewritten gate file: Pi (PiSession.swift:279-288, re-run every turn) and Command Code (the DROPPY_CODE_APPROVALS directory protocol). Launch flags only: Antigravity (AntigravitySession.swift:88 - see G8, the stored properties are never read back), the ACP `launchArguments`, and Copilot's `isExperimentalMode` which is a session-create parameter (CopilotSession.swift:130 `"isExperimentalMode": .bool(configuration.runtimeMode == .auto)`) - the source's own comment at :118-120 states that switching into or out of Auto restarts the session.
resolutions.port_impact: The port must not assume a uniform 'apply mode' path. Antigravity and the ACP launch flags genuinely require a process restart; Copilot requires a session restart only across the Auto boundary; Claude, Copilot (non-Auto), ACP, Codex, Pi and Command Code apply live. Document this once in the port so the UI knows which mode switches force a relaunch.

resolutions.finding: X7 (cross-cutting): how many providers can interrupt over the wire, and what replaces SIGTERM on Windows
resolutions.truth: The critic's own sentence is self-contradictory: it says 'Only two providers expose a cancellable, interruptible turn over the wire' and then lists five. SOURCE FACT, by counting every `func interrupt() async` in Services/Providers: FIVE send a wire message. ACPSession - `connection.notify("session/cancel", ["sessionId": .string(sessionID)])`, a NOTIFICATION not a request, preceded by answering every pending permission with `["outcome": ["outcome": "cancelled"]]`. CodexSession - `connection.request("turn/interrupt", ["threadId": ..., "turnId": ...])`. ClaudeSession - `control(["subtype": "interrupt"])`, preceded by denying every pending tool with `["behavior": "deny", "message": "The user stopped the turn.", "interrupt": true]`. CopilotSession - `connection.request("session.abort", ["sessionId": ..., "reason": "user_initiated"])`. PiSession - `process?.send(["type": .string("abort")])`. TWO have no interrupt message and terminate the process: AntigravitySession.swift:163-175 and CommandCodeSession.swift:229-235, both setting a flag first (`interruptRequested`, and Antigravity additionally `isStopping`) so `didClose` reports an interrupted turn rather than a crash. The source states the safety argument in comments: Antigravity's at :166-173 ('the conversation persists server-side for the next turn's `--conversation` resume'), Command Code's at :232-233 ('SIGTERM ends the run at once (exit 130); the CLI has already persisted every turn it finished, so the next `--resume` picks up from there'). An EIGHTH case is OpenAICompatibleSession (DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai), which has no child process at all - see G11.
resolutions.port_impact: Five wire interrupts port directly. For the two process-kill providers, Windows has no SIGTERM with delivery semantics; `TerminateProcess` is the practical equivalent and behaves like SIGKILL. That is acceptable for parity BECAUSE the source already relies only on server-side or on-disk persistence of completed turns, not on graceful shutdown - neither provider flushes anything on the signal. What must be preserved exactly is the flag-before-kill ordering, so the close handler reports `.interrupted` and the chat does not read 'Antigravity stopped unexpectedly'. Note the observable difference the port must accept: the source's exit code is 130 (SIGTERM-ish), Windows will report whatever exit code TerminateProcess was given, so any code that keys on 130 must be relaxed or the kill code chosen to match.

resolutions.finding: X8 (cross-cutting): MCP configuration reaches providers by several different channels from the same settings
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. Counting the distinct channels in the tree: SEVEN. (1) Claude: `if let mcpConfig = MCPProviderConfig.claudeConfigPath() { arguments += ["--mcp-config", mcpConfig, "--strict-mcp-config"] }` (ClaudeSession.swift:96) - both flags are passed together or neither, so with no connected server Claude reads its own config as usual (comment at :94-95). (2) Codex: `config["mcp_servers"] = servers` inside the thread params (CodexSession.swift:259). (3) Antigravity argv: `if !connected.isEmpty { arguments += ["--allowed-mcp-server-names"] + connected }` (AntigravitySession.swift:83-84) - the ids are appended as separate argv elements, not comma-joined. (4) Copilot: `arguments += MCPSessionOverrides.copilotArguments()` (CopilotSession.swift:486). (5) opencode: `environment.merge(MCPSessionOverrides.opencodeEnvironment()) { _, new in new }` (ProviderRegistry.swift:272). (6) Antigravity env: `if provider == .antigravity, let path = MCPProviderConfig.geminiSettingsPath() { environment["GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH"] = path }` (ProviderRegistry.swift:274) - so Antigravity uses TWO channels at once. (7) Pi and Command Code: `DROPPY_CODE_MCP_BRIDGE` plus `DROPPY_CODE_MCP_CONFIG` env vars read by the helper scripts (PiSession.swift:106, :109 and CommandCodeSession.swift:175, :178; consumed at PiCLI.swift:169 and CommandCodeAPI.swift:388). An eighth site reuses the Claude channel outside sessions: TextGeneration.swift:81 passes `"--disable-slash-commands", "--strict-mcp-config", "--permission-mode", "dontAsk"`. The critic missed one load-bearing fallback: CodexSession.swift:110-113 catches an RPCError whose message contains "failed to load configuration" OR "invalid transport" and, only when `params["config"]["mcp_servers"]` was set, retries the call with `config["mcp_servers"] = nil` - so a Codex CLI too old for a declared transport degrades to no MCP rather than failing the session.
resolutions.port_impact: Seven channels to implement and keep distinct; do not collapse them into one config writer. Windows specifics: the Antigravity id list must stay as separate argv elements (Windows command-line quoting will otherwise merge or mangle them), the two env-var channels must survive the port's environment construction, and the Codex mcp_servers retry-on-failure path must be reproduced verbatim including both substring matches, because it is the only thing that keeps an older `codex app-server` usable.

resolutions.finding: X9 (cross-cutting): two UserDefaults keys plus an alternate suite carry the provider cache, with a one-line migration
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, with line corrections. Keys: `cacheKey = "providerModelCatalogs"` (ProviderRegistry.swift:48, critic said 47) and `catalogDatesKey = "providerModelCatalogDates"` (:50, critic said 49), both on `UserDefaults.standard`. The third is `"recentSlashCommands"` on `(CaptureRun.defaults ?? .standard)` - read at :161 (critic said 158) and written at :698 (critic said 697), capped by `Array(recent.prefix(100))` at :697 with most-recent-first ordering (`removeAll { $0 == name }` then `insert(name, at: 0)`). Whole-blob rewrite confirmed: `updateCatalog` (:657-674) guards `!list.isEmpty, list != catalogs[provider]` (:667), then re-encodes EVERY provider's list into one dictionary and writes it: `let encoded = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: catalogs.map { ($0.key.rawValue, $0.value) }); if let data = try? JSONEncoder().encode(encoded) { UserDefaults.standard.set(data, forKey: cacheKey) }` (:670-672). Dates are written separately and also whole, by `storeCatalogDates()` (:537-542). The migration is at :167-173 (critic said 167-172), inside init, and exists only as that one map call: every cached row's `efforts` array is passed through `ACPSession.orderedEfforts` on load, with the reason given at :167-168 ('a list cached before the scales were ordered may still run high to low (Grok's did)'). `orderedEfforts` (ACPSession.swift:417 onward) ranks by a table: none 0, minimal 1, low 2, medium 3, high 4, xhigh 5, extra-high 5, extra_high 5, 'extra high' 5, max 6, ultra 6 - 11 keys, 7 distinct ranks - and leaves unranked values among their neighbours. All three persistence paths are suppressed under `CaptureRun.isEnabled` (:162, :176, :538, :669).
resolutions.port_impact: Two persisted keys and one alternate-suite key to carry over verbatim, since an installed build's existing data must still load. The whole-blob rewrite means the port must not do per-provider partial writes - a crash mid-write loses every provider's cache together, which is upstream behavior. The orderedEfforts remap must run on every load, not only once, because it is the only thing normalizing legacy rows; there is no version stamp on the blob. Reproduce the CaptureRun suppression so screenshot/capture runs never touch the user's real cache.

upstream_defects: ACPSession.swift:330-331 vs :338/:364 - applyConfigOptions resets `effortConfigID` and `fastConfigID` to nil on every call but does NOT reset `modeConfigID` or `modelConfigID`. Because the function also runs on the reply to the app's own `session/set_config_option` (ACPSession.swift:484), an agent that answers a model switch with a configOptions array lacking the thought_level or the `fast` model_config entry permanently drops the effort slider and the Fast toggle for the rest of the session: the guards at :456 (`let effortConfigID`) and :460 (`let fastConfigID`) then never fire again. Self-inflicted, triggered by the app's own request. Reproduce, do not fix.

AntigravitySession.swift:23-24, :57-58, :88, :150-151 - `runtimeMode` and `interactionMode` are assigned in init and on every send but are never read anywhere in the class; start() builds its mode flags from `configuration.runtimeMode`/`configuration.interactionMode` instead. A mid-thread Supervised/Auto/Full-access or Plan/Build change therefore cannot reach `agy` at all, and even a relaunch uses the original modes. The sibling properties `model` and `effort` ARE read back at :85-87, so the class applies half of its per-turn state on relaunch and discards the other half. Reproduce, do not fix.

CopilotSession.swift:456 - the fallback percent branch is `min(100, used / entitlement * 100)` with no lower clamp, while the primary branch is `max(0, min(100, 100 - remaining))`. A quota payload reporting a negative `usedRequests` produces a negative percent that reaches the usage bar. Asymmetric by construction; reproduce.

ProviderRegistry.swift:621-640 - refreshCredits has neither the 25-second watchdog nor the `defer` that refreshPlanLimits uses (:557/:559 and :569/:571), so a `CreditsReader.read` that never returns leaves the provider stuck in `loadingCredits` for the remainder of the run and its spinner never stops. It also has no forced-read queue, so a `force: true` arriving during an in-flight read is silently dropped at :622 (refreshPlanLimits queues it via `forcedLimitReads`, :548 and :584-587). Reproduce both.

ProviderRegistry.swift:627-630 - the empty-API-key path sets `credits[provider] = nil` and returns WITHOUT clearing `creditsFetchedAt[provider]`. The stale timestamp then makes the 60-second freshness gate at :631 suppress the very next read after a key is entered, so a just-pasted key can leave the balance blank for up to a minute. Reproduce.

ClaudeSession.swift:203-205 vs ProviderRegistry.swift:501-505 - `handshake()` throws "Claude could not load its commands." when the initialize response has no `commands` array, which also destroys the Claude MODEL catalog even though `loadClaudeCatalog` only reads `.models`. The failure is swallowed by `try?` and leaves no user-visible cause. Reproduce the coupling.

ProviderRegistry.swift:567 - `guard PlanLimitsReader.exposesLimits(provider), !loadingLimits.contains(provider) else { return }` re-checks two conditions already guaranteed at :547-548 with nothing able to invalidate them in between on the non-API-key path. A never-taken guard. Harmless; port it or drop it, but it is not a safety net.

PiCLI.swift:14-18 hard-codes the support-directory literal "Droppy Code/pi" while CommandCodeAPI.swift:443 and MCPBridgeSource.swift:243 interpolate `AppInfo.name`. A build whose CFBundleDisplayName differs from "Droppy Code" scatters its helper files across two different roots. Reproduce or resolve deliberately, but note the source is inconsistent.
dead_or_unreachable: PiSession.swift:285 writes `"systemPrompt": ""` into the gate file as a constant empty string, and it is the ONLY writer of that key (grep for `systemPrompt` in PiSession.swift returns just this line). The shipped TypeScript guards on it at PiCLI.swift:192: `if (typeof gate.systemPrompt === "string" && gate.systemPrompt.length > 0) extra.push(gate.systemPrompt);`. Because the length is always 0, that push can never execute in this checkout. PROOF: single writer, literal empty value, length-gated reader. The gate key must still be written (the reader does a typeof check) but the branch is dead.

AntigravitySession.swift stored properties `runtimeMode` (:23) and `interactionMode` (:24) are write-only. PROOF: exhaustive grep of the file yields occurrences only at :23, :24 (declarations), :57, :58 (init writes), :88 (reads `configuration.*`, not the properties), :123 (function parameter names), :128, :135 (uses of that parameter inside modeArguments), :150, :151 (send writes). No read of `self.runtimeMode` or `self.interactionMode` exists.

ProviderRegistry.swift:567 is an unreachable-failure guard: `exposesLimits(provider)` was already required at :547 and `!loadingLimits.contains(provider)` at :548, and between those and :567 the only path that inserts into `loadingLimits` (:556) is inside the API-key branch, which returns at :565 before reaching :567. PROOF: control-flow trace of refreshPlanLimits :546-581.

JSONRPC.swift:121 `respond(to: id, errorCode: -32601, message: "Method not found")` is the fallback when `onRequest` is nil. It is REACHABLE, not dead, but only on the short-lived probe connections that pass `configure: { _ in }` and therefore never install an onRequest handler (CopilotSession.swift:403, :429, :445; the CodexSession static probes). Every full session installs onRequest (ACPSession.swift:119, CopilotSession.swift:99, and Codex's equivalent), so the provider-specific messages at ACPSession.swift:557, CodexSession.swift:969 and CopilotSession.swift:775 are what a real session emits. Noted here because it is easy to mistake for dead code.

CopilotSession.swift:24 - the doc-comment claim that session DELETE was verified live is not backed by any code. PROOF: no `session.delete` or `session/delete` string exists anywhere in the DroppyCode tree; the only `delete` tokens in the file are that comment and the unrelated apply_patch header literals at :1037 and :1042. Stale documentation, not shipped behavior.
